Compares the element Id with the captured requested identifier.

Parses the ID/length header at the offset, checks the advertised additional-info boundary and dispatches known layouts by ID and length; unsupported layouts become a generic info element and truncated headers return null. Existing physical-array exception behavior is retained.

Creates a lazy iterator from cEMI raw data. The reviewed iterator advances by header plus payload length, skips null parse results and stops when fewer than three bytes remain in the advertised section.
Returns the first parsed element whose Id matches the captured requested identifier, or null.
Returns the first parsed element assignable to T through OfType and FirstOrDefault, or null.
Stores the supplied data buffer after a null check; does not clone it.
Allocates ID/length header plus payload and copies the stored data into the new cEMI additional-info block.

Initializes iterator state and captures the creating managed-thread ID.
Allocates the cEMI raw message buffer through the base constructor.
Wraps raw data and checks the two-byte header, advertised section length and item lengths. Existing edge behavior of the item-length loop is retained.
Reads the cEMI additional-info byte count at raw-data index one.
Enumerates parsed additional-info elements from this raw cEMI buffer.
Selects the first additional-info element assignable to generic type T.

Replaces matching equal-length payload in place. Otherwise removes the old item, grows the buffer and prepends a serialized item before service data. Existing byte-length overflow behavior is retained.
Finds the first item of the given ID, decreases the advertised length, shifts following bytes and shrinks the raw buffer; absent IDs do nothing.
Returns a writable span beginning after the two-byte cEMI header and advertised additional-info bytes.
Reads transmission band/mode from byte zero.
Writes transmission band/mode to byte zero.
Reads the high nibble of byte one.
Preserves the low nibble while replacing the high nibble of byte one.
Reads the low nibble of byte one.
Preserves the high nibble while writing the low four channel bits.
Reads the expected fast-ack slot count from byte two.
Writes the expected fast-ack slot count to byte two.
Reads reception band/mode from byte three.
Writes reception band/mode to byte three.
Returns the first byte of the selected two-byte fast-ack slot, or zero beyond stored slots; rejects slot indexes outside 0..63.
Returns the second byte of the selected fast-ack slot, or zero beyond stored slots; rejects indexes outside 0..63.
Tests bit zero of the validated fast-ack status byte.
Tests a short-ack bit for slots 0..63; valid slots beyond stored bytes return false.
Sets/clears a validated short-ack slot. Setting grows the buffer; clearing indexes current storage before trimming and can fail if that byte is absent. Preserve this behavior.
Counts set bits in the short-ack buffer.
Drops trailing zero bytes while retaining at least one byte.
Wraps 2..128 bytes of full fast-ack data. Rejects null and invalid size; retains the input buffer.
Wraps exactly four RF Multi info bytes. Rejects null and invalid size; retains the input buffer.
Wraps 1..8 bytes of short-ack bits and trims trailing zeros. Rejects null and invalid size; retains the input buffer.
Allocates enough bytes for the supplied BitArray, sets true slots and trims trailing zero bytes; SetAcked enforces the slot bounds.
